scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8873: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reports it cannot reach
anything outside its own subnet -- the server farm and the other pod all time
out -- though it still pings its gateway 10.1.1.1 fine. Oddly, when we logged
into switch_dist_1_1 itself, the switch CAN ping the server farm. Pod 2 is
unaffected. Find what broke.

injection.action: remove the OSPF network statement that advertises the pod-1 host subnet

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch_dist_1_1 OSPF configuration (missing
  `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` statement)
Mechanism: switch_dist_1_1 normally advertises the pod-1 host subnet
  10.1.1.0/24 into OSPF area 1; router_core_1 (the ABR) summarizes it into
  the area-0 backbone. With the network statement removed, the prefix is
  withdrawn everywhere, so the rest of the network loses its RETURN route to
  pod 1. The forward path still works -- switch_dist_1_1 keeps learning all
  remote routes over its uplink (172.16.0.6/31 is still in OSPF) -- so
  host_1_1_1_1's packets reach the farm and the replies are dropped on the
  way back: classic missing-advertisement asymmetry. switch_dist_1_1's own
  pings succeed because they source from its uplink address 172.16.0.7,
  which is still advertised.
Localization: switch_dist_1_1
Root cause: `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` removed from `router ospf` on
  switch_dist_1_1, so pod 1's subnet is no longer advertised
Fix: re-add the network statement on switch_dist_1_1 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
On switch_dist_1_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router ospf" -c "network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1"`
(`service frr restart` also heals it: the change was made only to the running
config, and /etc/frr/frr.conf still contains the statement.)
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: missing OSPF network statement / 10.1.1.0/24 no longer advertised
must-identify-mechanism: return-path failure -- the rest of the network lost its route back to pod 1 while the forward path still works
bonus-explains-gateway-anomaly: explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself still reaches the farm (pings source from its still-advertised uplink address)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a missing OSPF network statement on switch_dist_1_1: the Pod-1 access subnet 10.1.1.0/24 (interface br0) is not included in OSPF and therefore never advertised to the backbone routers.

**Mechanism:** switch_dist_1_1's FRR configuration contains only `network 172.16.0.6/31 area 1` under `router ospf`, covering only its uplink to router_core_1. The br0 interface (10.1.1.1/24), which is the default gateway for host_1_1_1_1, is entirely absent from that statement. As a result, router_core_1, router_core_2, router_core_3, and the server-farm subnet have no route to 10.1.1.0/24. Outbound packets from 10.1.1.2 reach their destination because switch_dist_1_1 forwards them over its OSPF-reachable uplink, but every reply is silently dropped: no upstream router has a return path.

**Why switch_dist_1_1 itself can ping the server farm:** locally-originated pings source from 172.16.0.7 (the eth0 uplink address), which IS distributed by OSPF and reachable from all routers. Transit traffic sourced from 10.1.1.x has no such advertisement.

**Why Pod 2 is unaffected:** switch_dist_2_1's running config includes br0 (10.2.1.1/24) as an active OSPF interface in Area 1, so 10.2.1.0/24 is properly flooded throughout the domain.

**Root cause:** The `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` statement (or equivalent `ip ospf area 1` on br0) was never added to switch_dist_1_1's OSPF configuration.

**Fix:** On switch_dist_1_1, add `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` inside `router ospf` (or run `ip ospf area 0.0.0.1` directly on the br0 interface). After the LSA floods, router_core_1 will install the route and bidirectional reachability from host_1_1_1_1 will be restored.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies switch_dist_1_1 as the affected device in the diagnosis.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: missing OSPF network statement / 10.1.1.0/24 no longer advertised
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names switch_dist_1_1 and states the `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` OSPF statement is missing so the 10.1.1.0/24 prefix is not advertised.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-mechanism: return-path failure -- the rest of the network lost its route back to pod 1 while the forward path still works
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly explains that the 10.1.1.0/24 prefix was not advertised so forward traffic leaves via the uplink but replies are dropped due to the missing return route (return-path asymmetry).

per_axis.axis: bonus-explains-gateway-anomaly: explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself still reaches the farm (pings source from its still-advertised uplink address)
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states that locally-sourced pings use the uplink IP 172.16.0.7 which is still advertised via OSPF, explaining why switch_dist_1_1 can reach the farm while 10.1.1.0/24 cannot.
The agent correctly recommends adding the 10.1.1.0/24 network to switch_dist_1_1's OSPF (or configuring OSPF on br0), which matches the expected fix.

The agent's log contains direct observations (OSPF interfaces, running-config, and remote route absence) that support the missing-network conclusion; the causal chain (missing network → withdrawn prefix → asymmetric reachability) is logical and the checks cover likely alternatives.
